we have measured UCN production in solid oxygen as a function of source temperature, and that we have used a combined $\chi^{2}$ analysis to extract UCN production and UCN upscattering cross sections from the measured data.
The measured UCN yield in solid oxygen is in good agreement with theory, and the excess UCN scattering is due to density inhomogeneities in the source material.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UCN production in solid oxygen is dominated by incoherent scattering, and that the UCN yield is proportional to the solid oxygen density.
the UCN production cross-section in solid oxygen is $\sigma_{\rm UCN} = 2.5 \pm 0.2$ $\times 10^{-6}$ b and that the excess UCN scattering cross-section is $\sigma_{ex} = 0.6 \pm 0,3$ b.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a UCN source in s-O$_ 2$ can be designed with a high UCN density and a low UCN loss rate.
UCN elastic scattering can be used to measure the density profile of the source, which in turn can be used to extract UCN production and transport cross-sections.
UCN production in solid oxygen is not limited by upscattering, but rather by the UCN transport length, which can be increased by reducing the source density and/or by using a larger cell.
